<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

The packed KV planner caps state buckets (sliding window, circular buffer, mamba) at the widest paged group. That can leave many narrow groups, each reserving its own blocks per request. This PR picks the block width that reserves the fewest bytes per max-length request. The current width is always a candidate, so the new grouping never reserves more per max-length request than the old one.

[#64120](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/64120) stacks on this PR. Its smaller records turn into +19% capacity instead of −9% with this fix; the projections are in #64120.

## Claims

- DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, stock FP8 KV: **+2.5% KV tokens** at the same memory, on real boots (eager 12,205,275 → 12,515,517; graph 11,747,853 → 12,052,038).
- Other packed-path models are unchanged: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (FP8 KV), DeepSeek-V4-Flash and MiniMax-M3.1-Flash get identical groups (table below).

## Validation

On MI355X (gfx950), image `vllm/vllm-openai-rocm:nightly-rocm100-5d35ce393`:

| Test | Result |
|---|---|
| `tests/v1/core/test_contiguous_kv_packing.py tests/v1/core/test_kv_cache_planning.py` | 92 passed (91 on main) |
| New `test_block_widens_when_it_reserves_fewer_bytes_per_request` on main | fails (SWA groups of 3 instead of 4) |
| New `tests/v1/worker/test_packed_kv_aliasing_round_trip.py` | 5 passed, on this branch and on main |
| pre-commit on the changed files | pass |

`pre-run-check` is a label gate for this account, so CI has not run yet. `pre-commit` and the tests above were run locally.

**Packed-path models.** Each row is a dummy-weight boot in which a hook runs both planners on that boot's layer specs and memory. On DSv4.1 the hook reproduces the real boots to within 0.1%.

| Model | Groups | KV tokens |
|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP1, FP8 KV, 64K | 9 → 7 | 11,745,002 → 12,043,541 (+2.5%) |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, TP2, FP8 KV, 128K | 6, identical | 14,356,239, identical |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4, FP8 KV, 64K | 5, identical | 1,241,057, identical |
| MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, TP4, recipe flags | 1, identical (layer-outermost, not packed) | 3,588,736, identical |
| `dots3_note`: **structural only, not booted** | n/a | n/a |

`dots3_note`'s backends are NVIDIA-only. Its `SlidingWindowMLASpec` layers take the new search only if their page size differs from its MLA layers', and the current width stays a candidate.

**KV aliasing round trip.** Dummy-weight greedy output can't compare planners (two stock boots differ at the first token), so the new test checks that no layer's cache overlaps another's. It plans and allocates with the real code, writes a distinct pattern per (layer, block) through each layer's cache view, and reads every layer back: each sees only its own pattern. On the real DSv4.1 TP1 specs, a one-off run gives 0 mismatches over 153 layer-blocks.

<details>
<summary>Packed-path table detail</summary>

| Model, flags | Layout | Bytes per block | Reserved per max-length request |
|---|---|---|---|
| DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash, TP1, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 65536 --max-num-seqs 256`, graph | BLHNC | 116,928 → 152,064 | 962.1 → 938.2 MB |
| Qwen3.8-Flash-Next, TP2, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --max-model-len 131072 --max-num-seqs 256` | BLNHC | 20,471,808 | 1,044.1 MB |
| DeepSeek-V4-Flash, TP4, `--kv-cache-dtype fp8 --block-size 256 --max-model-len 65536` | BLHNC | 917,568 | 12.47 GB |
| MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, TP4, `--block-size 128 --disable-hybrid-kv-cache-manager` | LBNHC | 5,898,240 | 48.3 GB |

- DSv4.1 boot setup: TP1 with `--load-format dummy` and `moe_intermediate_size` set to a TP4 rank's 576, so it fits one card. The engram tables are shrunk, which doesn't touch the KV layers.
- Qwen3.8-Flash-Next with an MXFP4 KV cache (an unmerged branch) wasn't measured.
- Round-trip test: both packed layouts (BLHNC, BLNHC) with DSv4.1-shaped FP8 and MXFP4 specs, each group given its own block IDs spread across the pool, plus a negative control that aliases two layers and must fail. The DSv4.1 one-off (64K, 32K in flight) gives 7 groups at 152,064 B per block here and 9 groups at 116,928 B on main, with 0 mismatches on both.
- Greedy: with vLLM's ±1e-3 dummy weights the logits are flat (top logprob −11.58). With norms at 1 and other floats at ±0.05 (top logprob −4.7), two stock boots still differ at the first token.
</details>

## Details

**Root cause.** Each packed group reserves `cdiv(max_memory_usage_bytes, page_size)` blocks per request. For a sliding-window group that's the window plus the tokens in flight: 1029 blocks at 64K with 32K in flight. Capping state buckets at a small anchor splits the 40 SWA layers into many narrow groups, each with its own 1029-block reservation.

**Change.** The grouping loop moves into `build_groups(block_bytes)`, unchanged apart from the cap's width. The candidates are the anchor plus every `k × state page` above it. The planner keeps the grouping with the fewest bytes per block × blocks per request, and ties keep the narrower block. It runs once at startup.

**Tradeoffs.**
- The objective is one max-length request's reservation, which is what bounds concurrency at `max_model_len`. The paged MLA group's per-block padding can grow.
- The choice depends on `max_model_len` and `max_in_flight_tokens`, so one model can group differently under different flags.

**Tests.**
- The new case covers the DSv4.1 pattern.
- Two cases that encoded the old cap at `max_model_len=16` now run at 65,536.
- `test_non_cacheable_swa_leaves_hits_to_the_paged_group` pins the new grouping: the paged group plus two SWA groups of 2, where main gives four groups of 1.

---

<summary> Pull Request Checklist </summary>

- [x] I used vLLM's `/pr-checklist` skill. (Mandatory for agents, optional for humans).
- [x] AI assistance was used during the creation of this PR.

- [x] **Design Fit:** Minimizes impact on core components, reuses existing functionality, and justifies added complexity. (Core file, 59 added / 28 removed lines, most of it the existing loop moved into a function.)
- [x] **Testing and Validation:** Validates the change and ensures any added tests are meaningful and reliable, with CI coverage or documented CI resource constraints and validation performed outside CI.
- [x] **Code Quality and Style:** Keeps code and comments clear and concise, and updates relevant documentation and examples.
- [x] **Pull Request Contents:** Includes a brief summary and relevant links, supports claims with evidence, explains root causes and implementation trade-offs, and follows the contributing guide.
</details>

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""KV aliasing round trip for packed DeepSeek-V4.1 groupings.
+
+Groups the layers with the planner, binds every layer's real cache view with
+``allocate_kv_cache``, and gives each group its own blocks, as the shared block
+pool does. A distinct pattern per layer, block and byte is written through each
+view; reading every layer back must return exactly its own pattern. A wrong
+stride, offset or alias between layers would overwrite another layer's bytes.
+
+CPU only.
+"""
+
+from math import lcm
+from unittest.mock import MagicMock
+
+import pytest
+import torch
+
+from vllm.config import CacheConfig
+from vllm.v1.core.kv_cache_planning import (
+    _get_kv_cache_bytes_per_block,
+    get_kv_cache_config_from_groups,
+    get_kv_cache_groups,
+)
+from vllm.v1.kv_cache_interface import (
+    KVCacheLayout,
+    KVCacheSpec,
+    MLAAttentionSpec,
+    SlidingWindowMLASpec,
+)
+from vllm.v1.worker.utils import allocate_kv_cache
+
+pytestmark = pytest.mark.cpu_test
+
+BLOCKS_PER_GROUP = 3
+NUM_BLOCKS = 64
+
+
+def _config(layout: str):
+    config = MagicMock()
+    config.cache_config = CacheConfig()
+    config.cache_config.num_gpu_blocks_override = None
+    config.cache_config.kv_cache_layout = layout
+    config.cache_config.block_size = 16
+    config.cache_config.enable_prefix_caching = False
+    config.cache_config.prefix_match_unit = None
+    config.cache_config.mamba_cache_mode = "none"
+    config.attention_config.hisparse_config = None
+    config.scheduler_config.disable_hybrid_kv_cache_manager = False
+    config.speculative_config = None
+    config.model_config.max_model_len = 65536
+    config.model_config.get_total_num_hidden_layers.return_value = 64
+    config.model_config.get_total_num_kv_heads.return_value = 2
+    config.model_config.get_num_kv_heads.return_value = 2
+    config.max_in_flight_tokens = 32768
+    config.parallel_config.pipeline_parallel_size = 1
+    config.parallel_config.decode_context_parallel_size = 1
+    return config
+
+
+def _dsv41_fp8_specs() -> dict[str, KVCacheSpec]:
+    """Stock fp8 records: 584 B main and SWA states, 132 B indexer."""
+    specs: dict[str, KVCacheSpec] = {}
+    for layer, ratio in ((2, 2), (8, 2), (14, 2), (20, 1)):
+        specs[f"layers.{layer}.attn"] = MLAAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=128,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=584,
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            tokens_per_state=ratio,
+            alignment=576,
+        )
+        specs[f"layers.{layer}.idx"] = MLAAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=128,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=132,
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            tokens_per_state=ratio,
+            alignment=576,
+        )
+    for layer in range(43):
+        specs[f"layers.{layer}.swa"] = SlidingWindowMLASpec(
+            block_size=64,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=584,
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            sliding_window=128,
+            alignment=576,
+        )
+    return specs
+
+
+def _dsv41_mxfp4_specs() -> dict[str, KVCacheSpec]:
+    """272 B MXFP4 compressed records beside 528 B SWA records: the planner
+    widens the block past the MLA group to fit 4 SWA pages per group."""
+    record_rows = lcm(528, 272)
+    specs: dict[str, KVCacheSpec] = {}
+    for layer in range(40):
+        specs[f"layers.{layer}.swa"] = SlidingWindowMLASpec(
+            block_size=32,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=512,
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            sliding_window=128,
+            state_content_bytes=528,
+            alignment=512,
+            block_stride_alignment=record_rows,
+        )
+    for layer, ratio in ((2, 2), (8, 2), (14, 2), (20, 1)):
+        specs[f"layers.{layer}.attn"] = MLAAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=64,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=512,
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            tokens_per_state=ratio,
+            state_content_bytes=272,
+            alignment=512,
+        )
+        specs[f"layers.{layer}.idx"] = MLAAttentionSpec(
+            block_size=64,
+            num_kv_heads=1,
+            head_size=68,
+            dtype=torch.uint8,
+            tokens_per_state=ratio,
+            alignment=512,
+        )
+    return specs
+
+
+def _pattern(view_block: torch.Tensor, layer_index: int, block_id: int) -> torch.Tensor:
+    n = view_block.numel()
+    seed = layer_index * 7919 + block_id * 104729
+    values = (torch.arange(n, dtype=torch.int64) * 131 + seed) % 251
+    return values.to(torch.uint8).view(view_block.shape)
+
+
+def _bind(specs: dict[str, KVCacheSpec], layout: str):
+    config = _config(layout)
+    groups = get_kv_cache_groups(config, specs)
+    bytes_per_block = _get_kv_cache_bytes_per_block(groups, KVCacheLayout[layout])
+    kv_config = get_kv_cache_config_from_groups(
+        config, groups, NUM_BLOCKS * bytes_per_block
+    )
+    views = allocate_kv_cache(
+        kv_config, torch.device("cpu"), KVCacheLayout[layout], None
+    )
+    # One sequence covering several blocks in every group, with each group
+    # owning distinct, non-contiguous block ids from the shared pool (block 0
+    # is the null block).
+    generator = torch.Generator().manual_seed(0)
+    ids = (torch.randperm(kv_config.num_blocks - 1, generator=generator) + 1).tolist()
+    assert len(groups) * BLOCKS_PER_GROUP <= len(ids)
+    blocks = {
+        gid: ids[gid * BLOCKS_PER_GROUP : (gid + 1) * BLOCKS_PER_GROUP]
+        for gid in range(len(groups))
+    }
+    return groups, views, blocks
+
+
+def _round_trip(groups, views, blocks) -> list[str]:
+    order = {name: i for i, name in enumerate(views)}
+    for gid, group in enumerate(groups):
+        for name in group.layer_names:
+            for b in blocks[gid]:
+                views[name][b].copy_(_pattern(views[name][b], order[name], b))
+    mismatches = []
+    for gid, group in enumerate(groups):
+        for name in group.layer_names:
+            for b in blocks[gid]:
+                if not torch.equal(
+                    views[name][b], _pattern(views[name][b], order[name], b)
+                ):
+                    mismatches.append(f"{name} block {b}")
+    return mismatches
+
+

+def test_every_layer_reads_back_only_its_own_pattern(make_specs, layout):
+    specs = make_specs()
+    groups, views, blocks = _bind(specs, layout)
+    assert sorted(views) == sorted(specs)
+    assert sorted(n for g in groups for n in g.layer_names) == sorted(specs)
+    assert _round_trip(groups, views, blocks) == []
+
+
+def test_round_trip_catches_an_aliased_layer():
+    """Negative control: bind one SWA layer onto another's bytes."""
+    groups, views, blocks = _bind(_dsv41_mxfp4_specs(), "BLHNC")
+    group = next(g for g in groups if len(g.layer_names) > 1)
+    victim, other = group.layer_names[:2]
+    views[victim] = views[other]
+    assert _round_trip(groups, views, blocks)
